problem: The old service silently selected the conversation baseline. The first repair also left four web choices as conversation replays rather than question tests.
change: All four new-run configurations now use a shared direct-question task and final-response delivery adapter. The UI requires protocol v3, blocks submission on older services and labels historical task types separately.

implementation.native: Selected native tools; no calculator; no event injection between model/tool steps.
implementation.agent-led: Agent-led tools, calculator, and boundary event updates.
implementation.frozen-baseline: Verified frozen source/tools/world with external question adapter and bounded durable failure recovery. Not an original frozen-baseline result.
implementation.progress: Current recovery plus request-local progress facts including delivered source results.

checks.name: HTTP, task mode, input fingerprints and final response projection
Direct runtime, source handling, recovery, progress and checkpoint behavior
Workers for all four choices, legacy alias, and original historical path
JavaScript syntax and capability/task-mode boundary assertions

comparison_conditions: All v3 runs use the same exact question, no supplied documents and the same fixed local model/profile. One run per configuration. Tools and orchestration differ. The earlier explicit-domain recheck changes the question and is diagnostic only.
result: All four v3 runs receive direct input and deliver a final response. All four still fail the intended modern LLM-harness concept check. Response delivery is fixed; concept knowledge is not.
limitations: The question is exposed development material; no held-out accuracy or latency improvement is established.
No domain tools or recovery feedback were used in the v3 concept runs. Scripted tests verify mechanics, not their benefit to answer quality.
Native tool capabilities differ from the agent-led variants; this is not an isolated ablation.
No live web retrieval or semantic quality gate. More prose is not evidence of a better answer.
Older server APIs still exist. The refreshed UI blocks their submissions; already-loaded old pages must be refreshed.
Historical records and frozen source remain unchanged; new adapted runs must not be merged into their original scores.
